title: Benzodiazepine: increases FREQUENCY of GABA-A chloride channel opening
vignette: A 25-year-old graduate student comes to the office for evaluation of anxiety. She describes episodes of sudden-onset palpitations, shortness of breath, and diaphoresis during which she wants to "run away before anyone notices." The patient arrives early for her classes to get a seat close to the door and has left during lectures due to feeling "out of control." There are no specific triggers for these events, but she is worried about having another episode next week during her final examinations. She does not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. Physical examination, ECG, and laboratory evaluation are normal. The patient is diagnosed with panic disorder. After discussion of treatment options, she decides to pursue cognitive-behavioral therapy and start a short-term anxiolytic medication that also has muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant properties. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of this medication?

clues.text: sudden-onset palpitations, shortness of breath, and diaphoresis
clues.note: Discrete, sudden surges of autonomic symptoms (palpitations, dyspnea, diaphoresis) are panic attacks, the core of panic disorder.
Panic disorder can be managed acutely with a short-term benzodiazepine (plus SSRIs/CBT for long-term care).

clues.text: short-term anxiolytic medication that also has muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant properties
clues.note: An anxiolytic that is ALSO a muscle relaxant and anticonvulsant describes a BENZODIAZEPINE - identifying the drug class and its GABA-A mechanism.

whatMatters: A short-term anxiolytic with muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant properties = a BENZODIAZEPINE. Benzodiazepines are positive allosteric modulators of the GABA-A receptor that increase the FREQUENCY of chloride channel opening (in the presence of GABA), hyperpolarizing neurons. Answer C. (Barbiturates increase DURATION; the two are classic opposites.)
strategy: Identify the benzodiazepine, then nail the GABA-A detail: benzodiazepines increase FREQUENCY, barbiturates increase DURATION of Cl- channel opening ('Frenzodiazepines' / 'Barbidurates'). Reject flumazenil (a GABA-A benzodiazepine-site ANTAGONIST/reversal agent), and the antidepressant reuptake mechanisms (SSRIs, SNRIs) - effective for panic long-term but not the muscle-relaxant/anticonvulsant short-term agent.

options.text: Antagonism at GABA-A benzodiazepine receptor sites
Increased duration of chloride channel opening
Increased frequency of chloride channel opening
Inhibition of serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake

eliminations.label: Antagonism at benzodiazepine site - flumazenil
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: blocking the benzodiazepine site on GABA-A = flumazenil, the benzodiazepine reversal agent. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: an antagonist would not be anxiolytic/anticonvulsant; it reverses benzodiazepines. ✅ Correct if: reversing benzodiazepine overdose (flumazenil).

eliminations.label: Increased DURATION of Cl- channel opening - barbiturates
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: increasing the DURATION of GABA-A chloride channel opening = barbiturates (e.g., phenobarbital). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: barbiturates increase duration, not frequency, and are avoided in anxiety due to fatal respiratory depression risk. ✅ Correct if: a barbiturate mechanism question ('Barbidurates').

eliminations.label: Inhibit serotonin + norepinephrine reuptake - SNRI/TCA
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: blocking serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake = SNRIs (venlafaxine) or TCAs. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: these treat panic disorder long-term but lack muscle-relaxant/anticonvulsant properties and take weeks to work. ✅ Correct if: a maintenance antidepressant for panic, not the short-term agent.

eliminations.label: Inhibit serotonin reuptake - SSRI (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: blocking serotonin reuptake = SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine), first-line for long-term panic disorder. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: SSRIs are not muscle relaxants/anticonvulsants and take weeks to act; the described SHORT-TERM anxiolytic with those extra properties is a benzodiazepine. ✅ Correct if: first-line MAINTENANCE therapy for panic disorder.

reasoning: Panic disorder treated with a short-term anxiolytic that is also a muscle relaxant + anticonvulsant = benzodiazepine
Benzodiazepines are positive allosteric modulators of the GABA-A receptor
They increase the FREQUENCY of Cl- channel opening (barbiturates increase duration)
-> increased frequency of chloride channel opening; answer C
mechanism: Benzodiazepines (e.g., clonazepam, lorazepam, alprazolam) bind a specific site on the GABA-A receptor - a ligand-gated chloride channel - and act as POSITIVE ALLOSTERIC MODULATORS: in the presence of GABA, they increase the FREQUENCY of chloride channel opening. Increased Cl- influx hyperpolarizes and stabilizes the neuronal membrane, making it less excitable - the basis of their anxiolytic, sedative, muscle-relaxant, and anticonvulsant effects. A key USMLE contrast is that BARBITURATES increase the DURATION of channel opening (mnemonic: 'Frenzodiazepines increase Frequency; Barbidurates increase Duration'). Because of dependence and tolerance risk, benzodiazepines are used SHORT-TERM (e.g., acute panic), while SSRIs/SNRIs plus cognitive-behavioral therapy are first-line for long-term panic disorder. Flumazenil is a benzodiazepine-site ANTAGONIST used to reverse benzodiazepine overdose. The reuptake-inhibitor options describe antidepressants, which treat panic but lack the muscle-relaxant/anticonvulsant profile and rapid onset described.
